title: Quadruply Bonded Mo2 Molecules: An Innate Emitter-Resonator Quantum System in Free Space
authors: Miao Meng, Ying Ning Tan, Zi Cong He, Zi Hao Zhong, Jia Zhou, Yu Li Zhou, Guang Yuan Zhu, Chun Y. Liu
abstract: In recent decades, significant progress has been made in constructing and studying individual quantum systems based on two level atoms (molecules) and photons. Here we demonstrate that the quadruply bonded Mo2 unit, with a MoMo bond distance as short as 2.1A, functions as an innate emitter resonator molecular quantum system capable of trapping visible light photons between the two molybdenum atoms under ambient conditions, thereby generating an intense quantized local electromagnetic field with an extremely small mode volume. The resonance fluorescence spectra of three Mo2 complexes indicate that the intermetallic Mo-Mo charge transfer transition is coherently coupled to the local scattering field, exhibiting vacuum Rabi splitting and Mollow triplets. Resonant coupling of single molecules and N-molecule ensembles to the scattered light through sideband excitation produces a sequence of discrete optical modes spanning a broad wavelength range, with polaritonic transitions identical to those observed in Ni2 based systems. These results establish the Mo2 molecule as an independent emitter resonator integrated quantum system that enables quantum optical experiments in free space using conventional spectroscopic instrumentation. This work extends quantum electrodynamics into molecular science, providing new insights into metal metal bonding, molecular physics, and light matter interactions.
summary: The authors demonstrate that the quadruply bonded $	ext{Mo}_2$ molecule acts as an innate emitter-resonator quantum system capable of trapping and strongly coupling with visible light photons in free space. By measuring resonance fluorescence, they observe characteristic signatures like vacuum Rabi splitting and Mollow triplets, confirming its utility for molecular quantum optical experiments.
main_problem: To demonstrate that quadruply bonded $	ext{Mo}_2$ units function as intrinsic emitter-resonator quantum systems capable of trapping and interacting with visible light photons in free space.
main_result: The $	ext{Mo}_2$ unit exhibits strong coupling signatures, such as vacuum Rabi splitting and Mollow triplets, confirming its role as an independent molecular quantum system analogous to established $	ext{Ni}_2$ systems.
method: Resonance fluorescence spectroscopy was performed on various $	ext{Mo}_2$ complexes using monochromatic UV light excitation across a range of wavelengths.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quadruply bonded $	ext{Mo}_2$ diatomic metal unit, which acts as an atomistic optical resonator. The behavior is analyzed using concepts from cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (QED), specifically resembling Jaynes-Cummings molecular systems.
key_observables: Vacuum Rabi splitting ($\Omega$), Mollow triplets/sidebands, and the observation of non-classical features like photon antibunching.
important_parameters: The system operates in the ultrastrong-coupling regime; key distances include the $	ext{Mo}-	ext{Mo}$ bond distance ($\approx 2.1 	ext{ Å}$).
main_assumptions: The observed quantum optical phenomena are attributed to the intrinsic resonator character of the diatomic metal core, allowing for testing against specific electronic configurations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate fluorescence spectra showing distinct emission features compared to conventional Stokes scattering, including Rabi doublets and Mollow triplets under varying excitation conditions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by comparing $	ext{Mo}_2$ to known quantum systems (like trapped ions or plasmonic cavities). It then presents experimental evidence via spectroscopy on multiple complexes, confirming strong light-matter coupling signatures characteristic of emitter-resonator interactions in free space.
why_interesting: This work directly extends cavity QED concepts into molecular science by identifying a robust, ambient-condition quantum optical element ($	ext{Mo}_2$) that can mediate strong light-matter interaction without requiring external high-finesse cavities.
